notes:
A big one. Everything below has been built and tested on one phone since the last release.

WHAT IS NEW

The helicopter actually flies now. It is launched last in the battle, which makes it the selected unit, and then the eye button hands control to it. Nothing has to recognise a helicopter, so it works with any aircraft, on any ship, on any map. It flies once at the start of a round and keeps being relaunched after that, as before.

It reads the screen now, not just pictures of it. The app can ask Android what is actually on screen - the buttons, what they say, where they are - instead of only comparing saved pictures. Used when it would otherwise give up and press Back. Pictures are still the fallback, and are still the only thing that works inside the game itself.

Controls are found by colour and shape instead of saved pictures. Buttons that used to be found by matching a photograph of them now get described by what they are - a solid blue block of this size, a white circle in that corner. Saved pictures break whenever the artwork or the background behind them changes, which has caused most of the faults this app has ever had.

FIXES

It no longer taps adverts and opens your browser. A Shoprite advert had a purple label behind its product name that was almost exactly the size and colour of the Increase reward button on the after-battle screen. The app tapped it, which opened the advertiser page, pressed Back, landed on the same advert and did it again - every nineteen seconds. The rule that finds that button now describes the real one precisely. Checked against 8929 recorded screens: it loses nothing and finds twelve real buttons it had been missing.

Advert close buttons get found properly. Google puts the X inside a white circle in the same corner on every rewarded advert. The app now looks for that circle. Across the whole screenshot history that finds 44 close buttons that were previously being missed, including on adverts with Install buttons on them, which it has never pressed and still cannot.

If a browser ever does open, it leaves immediately instead of sitting on it for eleven seconds.

The reward advert after a VICTORY is taken again. A win pays more rewards, which pushed the purple button lower down the screen and dimmed it, and nothing matched. One night that cost 57 of 76 reward videos.

The new Escort battle mode is recognised and played.

Modern Warships own Special Offer popups get closed. They used to stall a run for over a minute.

Over a minute of dead waiting per cycle removed. Waits now end the moment the screen moves on instead of always sitting the full time. Adverts are also skipped and closed sooner.

In battle, the app no longer loses control of the helicopter the instant the camera leaves the ship.

IN THE BACKGROUND

It keeps a written record of what happened - session times, game version, every stall and what it cost, and a ranked list of the screens wasting the most time. You never have to look at it; it travels out with the screenshots.

It tells you when it is stuck. Five minutes of recognising nothing raises a proper alert instead of the run quietly dying overnight.

It notices when Modern Warships updates and flags it, because twice now something has broken quietly after one.

Screenshots and the record upload themselves every twenty minutes, compressed, over mobile data. No cable needed. Screenshots are capped and trimmed so they cannot fill the phone. It never photographs anything that is not the game or an advert.

It notices when the game updates, records what phone it is on, and can update itself from the App version row on the front page.

The money counters are gone from the front page as requested; battles are counted instead.
